message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most famous American composers across different eras and genres:

| Era / Genre | Composer | Notable Works |
|-------------|----------|---------------|
| **Early American Classical** | William Billings (1746–1800) | *“New England Psalm”* |
| | John Frederick Dzeruniewicz (1795–1869) | *“American Hymn”* |
| **Romantic/Impressionist** | George Gershwin (1898–1937) | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| | Aaron Copland (1900–1990) | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| | Leonard Bernstein (1918–1990) | *West Side Story*, *On the Town* |
| **Modern/Contemporary** | Philip Glass (born 1937) | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks* |
| | Steve Reich (born 1936) | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| | John Adams (born 1947) | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **Film Scores** | John Williams (born 1950) | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| | Ennio Morricone (though Italian, he worked extensively in the U.S.) | *The Good, the Bad and the Ugly*, *Once Upon a Time in America* |
| **Jazz & Popular Music** | Duke Ellington (1899–1974) | *Mood Indigo*, *Take the A Train* |
| | Miles Davis (1926–1991) | *Kind of Blue*, *Bitches Brew* |
| | Bob Dylan (born 1941) | *Like a Rolling Stone*, *Blowin’ in the Wind* |
| **Contemporary Pop** | Max Martin (born 1971) | *“I Kissed a Girl”*, *“Shake It Off”* |

These composers have had a profound impact on both American and global music culture, spanning classical, jazz, film, and popular music.
